source_claims: Bailey says the long-marked vowels differ from unmarked vowels only in length, and unaccented lengths may be omitted phonetically although Oriental-language publications conventionally retain them. Breve-a is compared with English but; breve-e is approximately short e, probably lower; breve-o with hot; breve-u with pull rather than root, without usual lip protrusion or drawing together. These are attributed descriptions, not newly assigned IPA.

source_claims: Bailey says sonant aspiration is practically absent in Koci/Simla except probably through Hindi influence; postvocalic h is generally unsounded and the syllable has high falling tone. He contrasts northern/western Amritsar Panjabi devoicing and low tone. In discussing a proposed Romany–Shina connection he notes that northern Panjabi and Simla dialects except Bilaspur also avoid aspirated sonants. These are source claims, not asserted genetic or borrowing relations.
